header.running_head: Learning from Worthy and Reliable People and what Happens when Knowledge Lies with People Unworthy of it

Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi (RA) Travels to see Hadhrat Ali (RA) and the Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Concerning Travelling in Search of Knowledge

Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi (RA) says, "When I heard that Hadhrat Ali (RA) knew a particular Hadith, I feared that if he passed away, I would be unable to hear it from anyone else. I therefore embarked on my journey until I reached him in Iraq." [^2] Another narration adds that Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Adi (RA) said, "When I asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) about the Hadith, he narrated it to me but then made me promise that I would never report it to anyone else. I wish that he had not done that so that I could have narrated it to you people." [^3]

The statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) shall shortly be related in which he said, "If I knew of anyone who has more knowledge of Allaah's Book than I, I would definitely travel to him." [^4]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also said, "If a camel could take me to a person who has more knowledge of what has been revealed to Muhammad ﷺ than I have, I shall certainly go to him to increase the knowledge I have." [^5]
Learning from Worthy and Reliable People and what Happens when Knowledge Lies with People Unworthy of it
Rasulullaah ﷺ Sends Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba (RA) to Learn from Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) and Praises him

Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba (RA) says, "I once went to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request to refer me to someone who could teach well. Rasulullaah ﷺ then referred to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), saying, 'I am referring you to someone who will give you excellent education and teach you exceptional manners." [^6]
Another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Tha'laba (RA) added, "When I came to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), he was busy talking with Hadhrat
